question: Can I add my own stylesheets to override the default look? Do files need to be in a certain folder? Will my styles automatically override defaults or do I need to force them?
ground_truth: To add custom CSS to your Fern documentation, create CSS files in your `fern/` directory (they can be in subdirectories like `fern/css/` or directly in `fern/`). In your `docs.yml` file, specify the CSS file paths - you can add multiple files using list format: `css: [./css/header-styles.css, ./css/footer-styles.css]` or a single file with `css: ./styles.css`. The paths are relative to the `fern/` directory. Your custom CSS files are loaded after Fern's default styles, which means your styles will take precedence due to CSS cascade order without needing `!important` declarations (though you can use `!important` for extra specificity if needed). This allows you to override Fern's default appearance with your company's design system while maintaining the flexibility to organize your CSS files however makes sense for your project structure.

metadata.cited_context: You can add custom CSS to your docs to further customize the look and feel. Add a `styles.css` file and include it in your `fern/` project. In `docs.yml`, specify the path to the `styles.css` file: `css: ./styles.css`. You can specify any number of custom CSS files: `css: [./css/header-styles.css, ./css/footer-styles.css]`.
